name: netdata-cloud
footnotes: Same binary as the self-hosted row, claimed to Netdata Cloud. ML anomaly detection stays at its default (on).
kickstart's default channel is nightly; installed with --stable-channel so the version is a release readers can reproduce.

Anonymous telemetry and the daily updater timer stay at their defaults. The updater's unit is matched with the agent's; a unit that lives for less than the 10-second sampling interval is counted only as far as the samples catch it.

The three runs of this row were measured at the same time, on 2026-11-13/14 on box-2, box-4 and box-7, with a collector that records how much of the box's filesystem-metadata writeback the kernel charged to the unit. They are the third measurement of this row. The first runs, of 2026-11-07 to 11-11 (`data/2026/superseded/`), have no such record: their disk figures (231 to 276 MB per 24 h) include an unknown share of that stream. The runs that replaced them, of 2026-11-12/13 (`data/2026-slot5/`), carry traffic that the benchmark's operator caused (see the note on the Netdata Cloud Space below) and were measured again on the same three boxes. The rule fixed before each retest is that every run measured again replaces the run it stands for, whatever it shows, so all of this row's figures, not only the network figure, come from this slot and day. Against the medians of the runs of 2026-11-12/13, which were the published ones from 2026-11-13 until these runs replaced them: network 0.34 MB out and 0.19 in per 24 h (was 0.55 and 0.25), disk written 140.8 MB per 24 h (148.5), install time 25.7 s (30.2), CPU under load 2.9 % (3.2); the other figures moved by 1 % or less, except the kernel's whole charge of disk writes (233.3 MB per 24 h against 223.7) and the metadata taken out of it (90.3 against 75.2), which depend on how long the unit held the metadata stream. Against the first runs' medians: idle CPU 3.9 % (3.7) and CPU under load 2.9 % (2.8); the other figures, apart from the disk figures, are within 1.2 %. `docs/RUN-2026-slot6.md` and `docs/RUN-2026-slot5.md` have the causes and the rule.

Disk written counts data writes. Filesystem metadata is written through the block device's inode and is not counted for any row, whichever cgroup the kernel charges it to, and that includes the metadata an agent's own file activity causes. On a box running Netdata the metadata stream was 5.6 to 6.4 MB per hour (the six such boxes of the slot of 2026-11-12/13; 5.7 to 5.8 on the three boxes of these runs), on the three boxes without Netdata in the slot of 2026-11-12/13 2.8 to 2.9: about 65 to 85 MB per 24 h more, which Netdata's activity appears to cause and which is in no row's figure.

The disk figure is probably 10 to 16 MB per 24 h too low in each run. The record of the metadata writeback counts whole pages per pass and reads above what the kernel charges: by 11 % on a box where the two could be compared exactly, and by about 13 % (between 6 and 21 %) in the hours of the six Netdata runs of 2026-11-12/13. These three runs agree with those six where they can be compared: in the samples in which the unit was charged no more than the record shows, the charge is 88 to 90 % of the record. An hour's metadata is never taken out beyond that hour's charge, but this unit writes more than the stream in every hour, so the excess is not caught: 10 to 16 MB per 24 h in each run at 13 %, 5 to 24 MB over that range.

The Netdata Cloud Space the nodes are claimed to belongs to the benchmark's operator. In the runs of 2026-11-12/13 all three nodes sent more than usual at the same two moments, 20:06:50Z and 20:53:50 to 20:54:50Z on 2026-11-12, which raised this row's network figure from 0.3 to 0.6 MB per 24 h; when those runs were published the cause was not established. It was read on 2026-11-13 from Netdata's own access log on the three boxes: 53, 260 and 52 requests over the Netdata Cloud link, in those minutes and in no other, almost all for chart data, every one from the same signed-in user of the Space, with the role admin. The bursts were the operator looking at the Space's dashboard: a harness incident in this row. The three runs were therefore measured again with nobody opening the Space, and each box's access log was read after the collect and before any rebuild: no request over the Netdata Cloud link on any of the three boxes from the install to the collect (`docs/evidence/2026-slot6/`).
